findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct Scope to thread the op= label through lock.acquire/_acquire_once/_acquire_mkdir and set it at the store-write-lock acquisition site (compact_txn._compact_locked, lock.acquire at compact_txn.py:358), since compact_trigger.py acquires only a separate trigger lock and compact.py never calls lock.acquire.
evidence: compact_txn.py:358 `handle = lock.acquire(tracker, timeout=30, attempts=2, dual_window=True)` inside `_compact_locked` — this is the store write lock whose stamp `describe_lock_holder` renders and the incident is about.

compact_trigger.py:142-162 `_acquire_trigger_lock` opens `_trigger_lock_path` (a SEPARATE advisory file lock), and run_sweep STANDS ASIDE (returns) when `write_lock_is_busy` is true (compact_trigger.py:264-270) — it never itself takes the store write lock.

compact.py has no `lock.acquire`/`write_lock` call (search returned only `write_lock_is_busy` and `describe_lock_holder`); its compact-all path calls `_compact_locked` per ticket (compact.py:144), delegating the store-lock acquisition to compact_txn.py.

The store-lock stamp is written by `_owner._owner_stamp()` inside `_acquire_mkdir` (lock.py:345), reached from `lock.acquire` — so the op= label must be threaded through `acquire`/`_acquire_once`/`_acquire_mkdir` and set by the compact_txn call site, none of which appear in Scope.
findings.finding: The plan asserts the sweep's store-write-lock acquisition is in compact_trigger.py and compact.py, but the store write lock a blocked writer times out on is acquired in compact_txn._compact_locked (lock.acquire at compact_txn.py:358), which Scope omits.
findings.location: Scope — 'src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py, src/rebar/_commands/compact.py — set the label around the sweep's lock acquisitions'
scenarios: Implementer follows Scope, sets the label only in compact_trigger.py's trigger-lock stamp and/or compact.py, and the store-write-lock stamp (the one an actual blocked writer reads) still shows a bare pid — the exact incident the plan exists to fix goes unfixed.
The AC 'a sweep's real lock acquisition carries the label end to end' cannot be met because the real lock acquisition site (compact_txn.py) is out of scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the compact_trigger.py/compact.py scope line with the actual acquisition path: (a) add an optional label parameter to lock.acquire()/_acquire_once()/_acquire_mkdir() that flows into _owner._owner_stamp(); (b) set label='compact-sweep' at the compact_txn._compact_locked call to lock.acquire (compact_txn.py:358), tracing the sweep entry from run_sweep→compact_all_cli→_compact_locked so only sweep-initiated acquisitions are labelled.

findings.finding: The plan does not specify how the op= label reaches _owner_stamp from the sweep, and its Scope omits compact_txn.py where the sweep's store-lock acquisition actually happens. _owner_stamp() is invoked inside _acquire_mkdir (lock.py:345) via lock.acquire; during a sweep that acquire is called per-ticket at compact_txn.py:358 (inside _compact_locked), not by run_sweep/compact_all_cli. So 'set the label around the sweep's lock acquisitions' in compact_trigger.py/compact.py has no acquisition to wrap there — the data flow from sweep to stamp is incomplete.

scenarios: Implementer edits only compact_trigger.py/compact.py, finds no acquire() call to wrap, and either mislabels the wrong lock (the advisory compact-worker.lock, which is NOT the store lock the waiter reports) or leaves the store stamp unlabelled — so the LockTimeout still shows a bare pid

findings.suggested_fix: Introduce a contextvar in lock_owner (mirroring _seam._batch_sink) that _owner_stamp reads and appends as `op=<label>` when set; have run_sweep / compact_all_cli set it around the fold. This avoids threading a new parameter through compact_cli -> _compact_locked -> acquire -> _acquire_mkdir. Either way, add compact_txn.py to Scope since that is where lock.acquire runs during a sweep, and be explicit that the STORE mkdir stamp (lock.py) is labelled, not the advisory compact-worker.lock.

findings.finding: The Scope enumerates compact_trigger.py and compact.py as where the sweep 'sets the label around the sweep's lock acquisitions', but neither acquires the STORE write lock a blocked writer times out against. The sweep's store-lock acquisition is compact_txn.py:358 (lock.acquire(...) inside _compact_locked), which reaches _owner_stamp via lock.acquire -> _acquire_once -> _acquire_mkdir -> _owner._owner_stamp() at lock.py:345. describe_lock_holder reads exactly that stamp. The only _owner_stamp() call in compact_trigger.py (line 159) stamps the ADVISORY trigger lock (compact-worker.lock), a different file no store writer contends on. The inventory omits compact_txn.py and the signature-threading through lock.py's acquire/_acquire_once/_acquire_mkdir needed to carry op= to _owner_stamp — with no contextvar carrier existing to route around them.

scenarios: compact_txn.py:358 (lock.acquire inside _compact_locked): unpatched, so the store mkdir lock is stamped with a bare _owner_stamp() and the LockTimeout still shows only a pid for a sweep — the acceptance criterion 'LockTimeout names the holder as a compaction sweep' silently under-delivers.

lock.py acquire/_acquire_once/_acquire_mkdir: their signatures are omitted from Scope, so there is no plumbing path for op= to reach _owner_stamp at lock.py:345; the label set in compact.py/compact_trigger.py cannot reach the store stamp.
compact_trigger.py:159 (advisory trigger lock): patching this stamps the wrong lock file; a blocked store writer never reads it, so the label appears where no one times out.
findings.suggested_fix: Thread an optional op label through lock.acquire -> _acquire_once -> _acquire_mkdir -> _owner._owner_stamp(op=...), set it at the sweep's real store-lock acquisition (compact_txn.py:358 or a caller-scoped mechanism), and drop/qualify compact_trigger.py as a store-lock site — its _owner_stamp call only labels the advisory compact-worker.lock.

findings.finding: The plan introduces two related-but-distinct concepts — a labelled holder (op=...) and an 'optional' holder — without specifying how the renderer decides a holder is 'optional' and thus eligible for the safe-to-interrupt remedy text. AC line 2 asserts the remedy is present 'for a labelled optional holder' and absent for an ordinary writer, but the stamp design in Scope only mentions an 'optional op= field'. It is unclear whether optionality is inferred from the op value belonging to a known set (e.g. compact-sweep) or from a separate stamp field/flag.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that the remedy text is emitted when the op label is one of a defined set of known-interruptible operations (initially just the compaction sweep), and name that op value; or specify a distinct optionality marker in the stamp.
